subject: Atlas Health — Vector API latency surge following catalog rollout
messages:
From: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@atlashealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: Vector API high tail latency since this morning

Hi Aditya —

We started seeing a spike in vectorization latency and a handful of timeouts this morning across our production jobs. p95 is up from ~120ms to ~650ms and p99 is out >2s for the /v1/vectors endpoint. Throughput has dropped ~30% while error rate climbed to ~1.6% (mostly 504s).

I attached a sample of response timings and a screenshot of our dashboard. The timing window is 04:00–08:00 UTC. This lines up with the model catalog push we were told your team did overnight. Any insight on whether customers were remapped to a new model variant? This is affecting our search freshness job (nightly) and blocking a major release on our side.

Attachments: response_timings.csv, screenshot-logs.png

We need ETA for fix and whether a rollback is possible. If you prefer a quick call I can be available at 10:30 PT.

—Priya
Ops Lead, Atlas Health

Hi Priya — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I’ve looped in engineering (Laura) and SRE (Rishi). We’re triaging now.

Immediate plan:
- Rishi will pull the cluster-level metrics and check whether the recent model variant rollout changed kernel selection/quantization.
- Laura will check model routing for your account and whether any instances are pinned to new variants.
- I’ll coordinate a rollback if we confirm the catalog push introduced regressions.

We may need to revert the catalog entry for the affected variant; I’ll update you within 45 minutes. If helpful we can take that 10:30 PT call.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your deploy.

—Aditya

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@atlashealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: Vector API high tail latency since this morning

Quick update from engineering triage: we see a strong correlation between the catalog rollout at ~02:10 UTC (catalog v2026-11-29-02) and an increase in kernel context-switching on the hosted pool that serves Atlas. The rollout introduced a new model variant "vec-rl-quant-v2" which changes kernel selection heuristics for short-sequence inferencing.

Preliminary findings:
- P95 & P99 spike coincides with higher CPU wait on nodes handling mixed-size sequences.
- KV cache behavior differs for this variant; cache misses increase for short prefixes which amplifies per-request cost.
- Not all customers show the effect — those pinned to older catalog entries are unaffected.

I’ve attached a short tail of kernel logs (svc-kernel-logs.txt). Next steps:
1) Rishi to attempt a targeted rollback of the model assignment for Atlas' pool (not a full catalog rollback).
2) If rollback incomplete, we schedule full catalog rollback window (low traffic) and communicate timeline.

Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

[Attachment: svc-kernel-logs.txt]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: Vector API high tail latency since this morning

Triage details from infra:
- Grafana (last 6h) shows hosted-pool-3 (serving Atlas) CPU steal and increased kernel CPU wait starting 02:05 UTC.
- We executed a targeted model-routing revert for Atlas' tenant at 10:15 PT — preliminary telemetry shows p95 dropping from ~650ms -> ~180ms and p99 improving but still elevated.
- A small fraction (~7%) of Atlas traffic is still hitting the new variant due to sticky routing on long-lived connections; we’re invalidating session affinity for those connections now.

Mitigations applied:
- Targeted revert completed (10:15 PT)
- Invalidation of session affinity in progress (propagating)
- Warmup of previous variant to repopulate KV caches (ongoing)

We’ve opened INF-8421 for this and will attach heap/proc dumps if the p99 does not fully recover. Grafana: https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/vec/embeds?from=now-6h&to=now

Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Handoff notes/suggested actions:
- Provide Atlas a timeline for full remediation and an interim credit for downtime.
- Approve an SLA exception while we run a root-cause and harden rollout gating (canary thresholds, additional kernel validation).
- Prioritize a postmortem and share within 48 hours.

We should also consider a short-term change to our catalog rollout checklist to include a per-tenant simulation of sequence-length distributions.

Hannah Schmitt

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:04:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Atlas Health — Vector API latency surge following catalog rollout

Hi Priya —

Thank you again for flagging this. Quick summary and next steps from Redwood:

What happened:
- A catalog rollout introduced "vec-rl-quant-v2" which changed kernel selection for short sequences and increased cache-miss amplification for Atlas’ workload. This produced a P95/P99 latency regression for a subset of traffic.

What we did (timeline):
- 2026-11-29 02:10 UTC: Catalog v2026-11-29-02 rolled
- 2026-11-29 10:15 PT: Targeted model-routing revert for Atlas completed
- 2026-11-29 11:00 PT: Invalidation of session affinity and cache warm-up in progress

Current status:
- Telemetry shows p95 back near baseline (~140–200ms). p99 has improved but we continue to track residual spikes as cache warm-up completes.

Next steps:
- We will run a full regression postmortem and share within 48 hours (postmortem-draft.md attached).
- We will propose changes to the rollout checklist to require tenant-specific seq-len simulation and add an additional canary stage.
- Offer: We will issue a service credit for the impacted window and coordinate an executive-level review with Atlas if helpful.

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute handoff call tomorrow to walk through the findings and remediation?

Apologies for the impact — we’re treating this as a priority.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
